checks: Choosing an interior endpoint of the segment generically avoids the finite union of cones through lower-dimensional faces, so the exit is in a relative facet interior. The convex hull with the new point adds a genuine pyramid with volume at least c_0 t on its own fiber. In dimension one the same argument is interval extension.

The polyhedral ambient inequalities are violated by at most O(t) at the new point, with no violation of pure-base inequalities. Each old full-dimensional fiber has an interior point of positive slack for all nonzero continuous inequalities. Dilating about that point bounds the relaxed fiber and yields O(t) total added volume and convergence. The base projection and lattice-convex census are unchanged.

The gain at the interior base is a fixed positive fraction of the total. Its relative inball then gives a uniformly interior ball about each added mean. Because the compact projection is bounded, a fixed kappa sufficiently near one makes the associated loss means remain in a compact relative-interior subset. Exact moment correction gives a strict net mass gain and supported integer centroid base.

The uniform signed-cap estimate loses O(delta_t) from the fixed positive slack, because the outer source is bounded and the old finite-fiber section area bound is fixed. This includes pure-base caps. The true centroid is in the new convex hull, and its integer base is still one of the positive fibers.

For a proper base span, an ambient ball inside C can be chosen strictly on one side of a base hyperplane containing the span and within the positive distance to every other integer base in the compact projection. The hull agrees exactly above the old span and introduces no integer site outside it. Full base span already yields full ambient dimension.
